title: Our Lady of the Miraculous Medal: The Apparitions at Rue du Bac in 1830
summary: In 1830, the Blessed Virgin Mary appeared in Paris to St. Catherine Labouré, requesting a medal struck in honor of her Immaculate Conception. The devotion invites Christians to rely on God's grace, seek Mary's intercession, and live a life of prayer and charity.

blocks.text: 1. The Visionary and Historical Setting

St. Catherine Labouré entered the Daughters of Charity of St. Vincent de Paul at Rue du Bac in Paris in 1830. Her apparitions unfolded during political upheaval and anti-clerical sentiment in post-Revolutionary France.
Catherine kept her identity as the visionary hidden for decades while serving the elderly and poor. She died on December 31, 1876, and was canonized by Pope Pius XII in 1947.
2. The Apparitions of 1830 & Divine Dialogue
The first encounter occurred on the night of July 18–19, 1830, when Mary spoke to Catherine in the chapel about the trials facing France and the mission God would entrust to her.

blocks.title: Words of Our Lady to St. Catherine (July 18, 1830)
blocks.text: “Come to the foot of this altar. Here, graces will be poured out upon all persons who ask for them with confidence and fervor... Graces will be poured out especially upon those who ask for them.”

On November 27, 1830, Catherine saw Mary standing upon a globe with rays of light streaming from rings on her fingers, symbolizing graces given to those who ask. An oval frame formed around Mary with a golden inscription.

blocks.title: The Inscription around the Medal
blocks.text: “O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee.”

The reverse side showed the letter 'M' intertwined with a cross, resting above the Sacred Heart of Jesus crowned with thorns and the Immaculate Heart of Mary pierced by a sword, surrounded by twelve stars.
And Mary said, 'Behold, I am the servant of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word.'

Exegesis: Mary's response to God at the Annunciation is the foundation of Christian discipleship. The Miraculous Medal represents this same spirit of humble obedience and complete surrender to God's will.
3. The Meaning of the Medal: A Sacramental

The medal is a Church-approved sacramental—a sacred sign that disposes believers to receive grace. It is not a charm, talisman, or magical object. Its spiritual value depends on faith, conversion, and prayer.
The title 'Immaculate Conception' on the medal prepared Catholic hearts for the dogmatic definition of Mary's Immaculate Conception by Pope Pius IX in 1854.

blocks.title: A Sacramental, Not a Talisman
blocks.text: The Miraculous Medal is a sign of faith that prepares us to receive God's grace. It does not work automatically or magically; wearing it must be accompanied by prayer, the sacraments, and active charity.
4. Public vs. Private Revelation
Public Revelation was completed with the Apostles and contains all truths necessary for salvation. The events at Rue du Bac are private revelation.

blocks.title: CCC 67: Private Revelation
blocks.text: Private revelations do not belong to the deposit of faith. Their role is not to 'complete' Christ's definitive Revelation, but to help Christians live by it more fully in a specific historical era.
5. Investigation and Church Approval

Archbishop de Quélen of Paris authorized the medal to be struck in 1832. A canonical inquiry in 1836 confirmed the spiritual fruitfulness of the devotion. Pope Pius IX granted papal approval to the Miraculous Medal Association in 1847, and Catherine Labouré was canonized in 1947.

blocks.title: Church Approval Status
blocks.text: Episcopal authorization in 1832 and subsequent papal recognition validate that the medal is doctrinally sound and pastorally beneficial, without making the private vision a mandatory article of faith.
His mother said to the servants, 'Do whatever he tells you.'
Exegesis: As at Cana, Mary’s rays of grace on the medal point entirely to her Son. Her maternal intercession leads all believers directly to obedience to Christ.
6. Pastoral Application
Wearing the Miraculous Medal serves as a daily commitment to baptismal promises, frequent participation in the Mass and Confession, and service to the needy.

blocks.title: Central Lesson
blocks.text: The Miraculous Medal reminds us that all grace comes from God through Jesus Christ. Mary intercedes for us and teaches us to open our hearts to God's love in prayer and service.

blocks.title: Closing Prayer
blocks.text: O God, Father of mercies, you prepared the Virgin Mary to become the Mother of your Son and a model of discipleship. Through the intercession of the Immaculate Virgin and St. Catherine Labouré, deepen our trust in Jesus Christ, our sole Mediator. Help us use this medal as a sign of your love and a call to holiness. O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee. Amen.
